title: A Case of False Advertising
text:
White Lion describes the contents of the packets as sugar and honey. Unfortunately, they are not forthcoming about the percentage of each ingredient. For all we know, it can be 99% sugar and 1% honey. At 10 cents for a small packet (if you buy the case of 500), it's a lot to pay for honey-flavored sugar.

Incidentally, the packets I bought have a notch cut into one end that makes them quite easy to open. The slim packets contain a very small amount of sweetener that has little sweetness or flavor. This product may be nothing more than a clever case of false advertising: selling sugar for the price of crystalized honey.

title: These are not salted - no sea salt (or perhaps a negligible amount) is present on the nuts themselves as packaged
text:
I was very concerned about all of the mention of sea salt with these nuts, both in the description here on Amazon and on the packaging holding the nuts when they arrived. This made me think that they were salted, making them junk food and not a healthy snack.

Fortunately, they are NOT salted. The sea salt that is mentioned is just part of the soaking process to get the nutritionally destructive phytic acid out of these things. They are then probably washed again to get all of the salt off because I do not taste any significant amount of salt on them when I eat them.

I was considering subtracting a star because the skins have been removed from the nuts. We now know that approximately 90% of the phenols in walnuts are found in the skin, including key phenolic acids, tannins, and flavonoids. However, I think that the sprouting and soaking process may require that the skins be removed, so I am giving them the benefit of the doubt.

title: Smurfberry Cereal- in a coffee!  It's delicious! UPDATE!!!!
text:
[[[[[[UPDATE]]]]]]]
I’ve happily enjoyed 4 orders of Crave flavors since the first review. The latest box I got, an entire box of blueberry vanilla, is just plain awful. I’m not sure who Crave is trying to fool here. Each kcup was significantly lighter in feel. Those of us that are loyal to brands of kcups get to know the heft and rattle of each brand we like. These were so off, I had to break out my scale. Of the 8 I bothered to measure, all but one showed up a a bantamweight 13 grams. (The outlier had 14 grams.) For comparison, I popped on the kcup from my local roaster and I was 21 grams. That’s a little unfair I though, since it’s a local vendor, so I opened a box of Peet’s, and the 8 I pulled out were 19 grams.
Shame on you, Crave! Did you think we loyal drinkers wouldn’t notice??? Way to ruin a good thing!

<<<<<<<original review>>>>>>>>

For those old enough to actually remember sitting down to watch real Saturday morning cartoons with a ridiculously huge bowl of sugared goodness and milk--- this coffee (which they call "Blueberry Vanilla") is the EXACT flavor of Smurfberry cereal. I was completely dubious about brewing it up- it was one of the ones in the variety pack I figured would be an "also appeared..." Alas- the first waft of berry deliciousness that came from the still-brewing cup- I rushed back over to grab it as soon as it was done. The scent- the flavor- it all brought me right back to candy-colored animation with cartoon-colored breakfast foods with shag carpets and 3.5" action figures... Childhood in a cup.
Totally came back just to buy more of the standout! (The others were really good, by the way: the butter toffee is awesome, and the Vanilla and Caramel are strong contenders, too.)

title: Helped to Stop My Son's Asthma
text:
I purchased this to help with my 9-year-old boy's asthma. It has 10,000mg of omegas which in my opinion is insanely high and awesome.

Our family eats organic, we all take vitamins, we know our deficiencies, and we know our intolerance's and stay away from those things. With that said, my son has been dealing with inflammation and asthma from that inflammation since May of 2017. We have managed to treat him homeopathically and he has not needed to use his inhaler EVER♥. He usually wheezes at night and in the morning with occasional issues during the day when he is not on point with his diet. He does have a dust intolerance, we live in Arizona, so there is little we can do about that.

Anyway, we have had him on a strict diet with vitamins for his deficiencies as well as vitamins to help with his breathing issues for a while. He takes D-Hist & NAC as well as a probiotic for his gut. We just moved him to an adult probiotic that is stronger as well as an adult men’s multivitamin that we cut in half. He just learned how to swallow vitamins so we are moving away from kid’s vitamins. We were very strict for 3-4 weeks, trying to get a handle on the wheezing to get it to stop before school. While all these things had helped and it was better, he was still wheezing at night and in the morning. :( Mommy (me) was completely upset about the inability to get him to stop wheezing though healthy means.

I started this oil on Saturday 7/21/18. It is HARD to take. He wanted to do 15ml straight. We tried that and he got it down but he gagged. We decided to split up the does and do 7ml in the morning and 7ml at night but again he gagged. We then bought some organic vitamin D orange juice and mixed the hemp oil in a ½ cup in a mason jar so we can shake it and that seemed to do the job and that is what works and what we are currently doing. The sugar content is 10g in that dose with the orange juice but since he eats protein and fats for breakfast only with no sugar, I thought this was a happy medium he could maintain every morning. Again, my son is 9, not into salads or juicing that much so this was doable for long term success.

The results were AMAZING. By Sunday, 24 hours after his first dose, his nighttime asthma was gone and by Monday morning he was perfectly fine with no symptoms. This had been something he was dealing with for 15 months and in 24 hours it was gone! 2 weeks later and he has been amazing! The only flare up he had was after he went to a birthday party and ate 3 slices of pizza. Which he is intolerant to dairy, wheat, soy, coconut oil, starch, red dye #5 likely in the sauce. So at night he was wheezing but by the next day his body was 100% recovered. ♥

I do want to note that while this is a partial fix, he is still having drainage issues and inflammation so we are still working on things to correct his allergies. Currently he is seeing someone though AAT hoping that will help. At least we have a HUGE part of the puzzle fixed, now if we can get his constant runny nose fixed we should be all the way out of the woods.

So blessed by this hemp oil. To hear your son, who has been wheezing for 15 months, sleep soundly breathing clearly naturally is such a good feeling. ♥

title: High quality, but not organic for the price
text:
This is a brand I've purchased many times before, though not the avocado oil. When you need a high heat oil for grilling or high-temperature roasting in the oven, something like avocado oil is a great choice. I've recently used it on some meats (pork and chicken) and fish for grilling - where I didn't want grill flames going crazy from the high heat.

The metal canister keeps the light out and also looks nice if you choose to set it out in your kitchen. The canister I received had an expiry date two years out (good) and noted it was a product of Mexico (no surprise there.)

This particular version is not organic. It's also not "delicate" -- this brand also sells this variety, and I'm not quite sure what that difference means. How much better is it than the generic Amazon brand sold, also non-GMO? Honestly, probably not a whole lot, and I assume you're paying for the metal container and the high reputation of the brand. But for this price, I'd nearly expect it to be fully organic. Nonetheless, it also appears there isn't much available for organic avocado oil anyways.

I generally don't use avocado oil to produce a strong taste lift in something -- in which you might consider olive oil -- as you'll find the taste quite mild. And no, I don't think it actually tastes like avocado, either.

So if you want a known good avocado oil, and perhaps even want to give this nice looking bottle as a gift, you've got a winner. But other brands will probably suffice for less.

title: Not the best, but you get what you pay for ... and what is that hard clump in the jar?
text:
I'm kinda disappointed in the quality of this product - even for the price. There was a hard clump of stuff inside it, as if it wasn't
churned enough, or has been sitting on the shelf for a LONG time. It was hard for me to remix, unless I put it in a food processer. I ended up breaking it up with a fork, and putting about a tablespoon in the smoothies I make for breakfast instead. I will continue to order this for the price range - because now that Almond butter has become so popular - it seems the pricing is going up. Oh Come on now... really? ( I won't buy peanut butter due to allergies)

So my rant is this - in a country that has manipulated the food system so badly - we now have to pay a premium to eat healthy?
I know that thinking stinks in my mind - when manufacturers have the means to grow things without all the doo-daa's that are going into our foods. We have all lost what living really is suppose to mean - instead Society is focusing on attaining big houses, big cars, lotsa stuff - and we think that is Living? Life is hard - that is a fact and has been since mankind's been on this earth. We would work the soil with the sweat of our brow and so on...

But for the most part - we will continue to suffer the affects of food that has been altered, gmo'd, and sprayed to death - so for that, we will continue to pay the price, right?

So, my money has to go into extending a better life physically than worrying about what I am to wear each day - after all, how much do we really need?

Next is the inconsistent degree of freshness from bag to bag in a box of a dozen bags. Many bags are filled with chocolate that has turned whitish and bad tasting. This product is obviously too old to be sold. At this price, I expect fresh product at lest. But the highest price paid for these is putting the sugar substitute Maltitol in your body. I am not easily turned off by artificial ingredients or even GMO's. Most are fine for consumption and GMOs held the promise of feeding many more people. But the Maltitol used to replace sugar in this chocolate is simply bad to put in the body. Number one is that it acts as a laxative in many people. Not in everyone, but in enough people that it is definitely more than a few percent. If you've had your gall bladder removed or have any existing GI problems, avoid these at all costs. The other thing to note is these are not low calorie as you might expect without sugar. From Healthline.com: "After eating maltitol, some people experience stomach pains and gas. It also can act similarly to a laxative and cause diarrhea. The severity of these side effects depends on how much of it you eat and how your body reacts to it." Depending on the article you read, you will find more information on other health concerns with this product. It does affect glucose and carbohydrate metabolism and needs to be monitored.
Considering that half the bags I've received are whitish because they are so old, I'd avoid this product.

title: Good Cup of Joe... Edited Review
text:
Below, you will see my original review. After talking to several other Keurig owners, I decided to return my unit (k250). The water & coffee grounds were overflowing over the top of the cup. With the new unit I only get a very small amount of sediment at the bottom of the cup. With this in mind, I am bumping up my rating from 3 to 4 stars.

When I ordered this coffee, I was hopeful that I would have finally found a solution to coffee grounds in my cup. Unfortunately this was not the case. In theory, these cups should have worked. They have a filter unlike the traditional "K" cup and the bottom needle does not puncture a hole. The water should flow through the filter as it would in an automatic drip coffee maker. As I took my first few sips I thought, not bad. As I finished the cup, there they were, grounds in the bottom of my cup. Maybe this is just an inherent flaw of the Keurig coffee makers and for some this is not a big deal. For me, I like to finish my cup of coffee.

I purchased this brand based all of the 5 star reviews & questioned answered regarding the issues of grounds in the cup. Many have said that this issue had been resolved. Well I'm telling you it hasn't.

As a side note: Before brewing my first cup with these K cups, I cleaned all of the components to ensure there was no residual grounds left from my previous brewing method of using the "My Kcup" and my own coarsely ground coffee.

title: Good quality chia seeds
text:
No complaints about these chia seeds. They are fresh and perform exactly as they should. I use them as an add-in for baking, especially muffins and hearty cookies. I soak the seeds in water for about 30-45 min (although it can soak for much longer including leaving the container in the fridge for overnight soaking) until the seeds form a gel-like mass. They add a nice, subtle crunch to the muffin/cookie/etc. that I find very enjoyable. The seeds also have a pretty good nutritional profile, which is also a benefit of including them.

The soaked seeds can take the place of eggs in baked goods (sometimes the seeds are called "vegan eggs"). I find that 100% substitution for eggs makes for a too-dense final product, but replacing 1/4 to 1/2 of the eggs with chia comes out pretty well (although still a bit more dense).

The pouch is sturdy and can be resealed, although it's best to store the seeds in an air-tight container (I prefer glass) once the pouch is opened. The pouch I received in April 2021 has a use-by date of Oct 2022.

title: Delicious Double Shot That’s Full Flavored w/ Cocoa & Caramel Notes, Smooth & Creamy-Better Value
text:
Nespresso Double Chiaro capsules brew a double espresso shot (3.4 oz) for VertuoLine machines only. This is delicious medium roast espresso. It rates an intensity 6 and I usually favor higher intensity espressos, but Chiaro is so good it’s among my favorites. It’s not as bold and lacks the bitterness of the more intense espressos like Altissio and Diavolitto, but it’s rich and full flavored with dense and creamy body and good crema. This is a smooth and balanced espresso but not bland or weak.

Chiaro makes a delicious and satisfying latte, so I don’t even miss the premium coffee chains. When I add steamed milk and sugar (or honey or Jaggery), I taste cocoa notes with a hint of caramel that’s perfect for my morning latte. I typically use two espresso capsules that brew 1.7 ounces at a time, so this double espresso capsule for just $.15 more is a great value by comparison. I’ll definitely buy Double Chiaro espresso and trade off with my higher intensity favorites. Love it. 5 stars.

title: Good Flavor, Good Size, Soft Paper
text:
Our 2.5 year old son loves these and they're a good quantity to last a while at a reasonable price. Here's the essentials
Pros: They taste really good and have actual flavor and aren't just colored sugar. Thus, when your kid sucks on it and drops it on the floor and you decide to bite the bullet and do an emergency parental "cleaning" before handing it back, you'll be glad you did, except for the dirt and rocks bit. But, let's be honest, that's not the lollipop's fault. Your kid will enjoy them, so they make a good "if you this, then you get that" incentive/reward/treat and can be just the thing to stop a mid-store melt-down, or disrupt that mid-car trip moment when your child realizes they forget that essential favorite toy. The lollipops are big enough to be a little treat but not so big I worry about overloading my son on sugar or anything like that by just having one or two in a day.

Cons: Your kid will decide to learn to climb up on a stool and open the cookie jar to get them without asking. Also you'll find this out on sucker 2 or 3 if you're not careful.
The paper sticks are a bit on the soft, moisture absorbent side, so when your kid finally learns to lick them instead of crunching them to bits right away, you'll be so proud you taught your kid to enjoy the finer things, but you'll also be a little sad because that essential parental cleaning after a drop is a little grosser with a wet soggy, folding over stick. ;)

title: Tasty Carob malt balls, even if the claimed serving size is ridiculous ("1/4th of one ball" is a serving.)
text:
Carob flavored malted milk balls taste fine, and are (I'm told) slightly healthier than regular chocolate, in addition safe enough that I can give one or two to my dogs without the concerns for regular chocolate (which is NOT safe for dogs). My only minor quibble is with the label's information as to the nutritional values. It says there are about 120 malt balls to the pound/package, which looks about right. However, the label also says that
there are 454 (Four HUNDRED and fifty four!) servings per package. So if you do the math (120 balls in a pound, divided by 454 servings per pound bag), you find their concept of a single serving is 1/4th of ONE malted milk ball. Oh, yea, sure. "I'm hungry, I'll make myself a serving of malted carob balls. I'll just cut ONE ball into quarters, and eat ONE of those quarters, and put the other 3/4ths back in the bag. Mmmm, now I'm stuffed." Not in this world. The package comes from Canada, but even accepting the perception that Americans tend to overeat, I don't see "one 1/4th of one malted milk ball" being a serving in any country on Earth. Could be a typo, perhaps. So....ignore the label, eat a handful.

title: Don't over consume a Neutral or alkaline water. Still a lot of positive benefits (get PH strips)
text: This water has a PH of 7.4.. The body has a normal PH of 7.35 to 7.45, so in comparison to the PH of an arterial blood gas 7.4 IS NOT alkaline.. In comparison to many other waters yes it is more alkaline, but 7.4 is considered neutral or "base". On the other hand if you have a very alkaline diet intake, this water is still really good, but I would limit my intake or be smart and pay $3 to $5 for a bottle of 100 urine PH strips and confirm and close good approximation of your PH, the bottle has a color chart to quickly get a reading. No it's not an Abg, but it gives you an idea. 80 to 90 percent of Americans have a significantly acidic diet, so many people can and do benefit from a Neutral or occasionally a high alkaline water. There are waters that are sold at the gas station with a PH of 9.5+. That is very alkaline! That it something I drink when I know my PH is low. Diabetic patients can benefit from consumption depending on there glucose levels. People with heart burn definitely can benefit. I still wouldn't consume a large amount of even a Neutral PH water like this without checking my PH. A good thing comes along and some people (may or may not) find a way to overdue it & then have a plethora of negative things to comment about it without doing a miniscule amount of research on it. Really good water though, no after taste and very smooth. Perfectly packaged also..

title: Tea: Clipper Teas Everydays Organic Tea
text:
I had been consuming Clipper Organic Green Tea for months. The local market discontinued the product and brought in other teas that were not organic which I do not generally consume. I began searching for organic teas on the internet, only to find that there are many available. Vey few though that engage in the total business culture to preserve and protect the planet and its occupants, and Clipper apparently has been doing this for many years.
Since I was purchasing my organic green tea by Clipper Teas, I decided to try some of their other offerings, including the Organic Earl Grey and the Organic Everydays Tea. I am more than pleased. I love the flavor of all of the teas I have tried. I even began to make a latte by adding almond milk, cinnamon and Agave Nectar or honey to the Organic Everydays Tea and it turned out wonderful.
I have only been on my specific plant-based diet geared toward ultimate health and I wished to drink something with more health attributes than water, though water is essential in its own way. This tea is a great addition to any ultimate health oriented diet whereas a person wishes to receive the many antioxidants available in organic teas.
Additionally, I also try to make my purchases from companies engaged in Fair Trade Standards and the directive to only purchase from farms using renewable methods, water conservation and fair pay ethical standards.
I love your teas and salute your efforts to keep this world safe and better for humanity.
Sincerely,
Frank B Howard

title: DON'T DO IT
text:
I'm a broke college student. Between working and going to school (both full-time), coffee is kinda like a major food group to me. This is not coffee, at least not in any form I recognize. I read the reviews, and saw that although the product wasn't meant to work in a Keurig 2.0, they included a clip to make it work. I decided to go for it.
Upon receiving my box, I opened it to retrieve the nectar of the gods known as coffee, and saw the purple plastic clip in the box. I took said clip out of the box and examined it. It was so cheaply made that there were already weak points in it. I wondered how it would make it through the entire box, but put it in the Keurig.
Then I popped my first pod. Something resembling weak coffee dripped into my mug. Dubiously, I took my first small sip. I'm glad it was a small sip and not a full on gulp.
After trying all of the various flavors, I came to an astonishing conclusion: it is, in fact, possible to make a cup of "coffee" even I don't like. It was so weak, I tried to use 2 pods on the smallest setting, all to no avail. Every flavor was weak, and some of them were just undrinkable, particularly the "cream" flavors. Do yourself a favor and stay far, far, away from Infusio, because crappy coffee is worse than no coffee at all, if only because it's a tease.

I had saved a piece of my old local tried-and-true brand, and I used it to compare it with this one. After carefully unwrapping this last week I was dazzled by it's robust flavor. It's the real deal! And it grates like a dream. I find I need less of it because of it's potency. This three pound slab should last quite a long time. title: 1150 or 240 that is the question!
text:
C. Rust is correct, the bags do contain a little less tea as they are designed for those who make tea by the cup instead of the pot, something (shock horror :^) the British have begun to do more often. We also discovered this when we first brought back several of these bags from Costco in Manchester England. I too wondered if it was worth it as it does take 3 to make a pot whereas the 240 count box size only takes 2 so I did the math and found that it was still worth it to get the 1150 bags. I just did the math again using the US price on Amazon (yes, we are running out and no trip to the UK in the near future) and it is still cheaper to buy the bag of 1150 bags versus the box of 240 bags.

The box of 240 is $0.77/oz based on the weight of the tea in the box. The bag of 1150 is $0.55/oz. But even if you just do the math with the number of tea bags used it is still cheaper. The box of 240 at $19.95 a box is $0.08/bag or $0.16 a pot if you use two bags a pot. The bag of 1150 at $48.95 is $0.043/bag or $0.13/pot when you use 3 bags a pot.

BTW, a box of 240 at Sainsburys in the UK costs $9.48 today but if you factor in the airfare to go and get it I guess we're still getting a bargain here :^)

title: A great tasting option to conventional flour
text:
I decided to try spelt flour after reading some disturbing information regarding the unimpressive nutritional value of "dwarf wheat," a.k.a. regular ol' wheat flour. Thus far I have been very impressed, and VitaSpelt has completely replaced conventional flour in my kitchen.

So far I've adapted recipes for chocolate chip cookies and several types of yeast bread. You will find that the gluten in spelt (as mentioned on the label) is more delicate so it's important not to overwork yeasted doughs. In general, I've found that you want to increase the ratio of flour to moisture for good consistency. For example, in adapting the standard Toll House cookie recipe, I add another egg and 50% more flour and get delicious, chewy cookies.

Spelt also seems to cook more quickly and burn a bit more easily. To give a good idea to anyone who isn't terribly comfortable monkeying with recipes, I made the following changes to the Toll House cookie recipe.

50% more flour
1 extra egg (50% more)
bake 8 minutes exactly at 350 instead of 9-11 minutes at 375

I hope this helps!

title: Revised 1/19/2015: Odd Earthy Taste
text:
Revision to the original review:
When I first opened the bag, I had to try it because of all of the 5 star reviews and was exited to try it. But, as described below, I didn't like the taste so much because it was odd, and unfamiliar. But for some crazy reason, after the bag has been opened for over a week, that weird taste has gone away, revealing a much better taste! It is fairly smooth and a great everyday coffee. It is also possible the taste could have been as a result of the creamer I use, but unlikely because I didn't taste it in the other coffee I had been using. So I had gave it another star because it does now taste better, but left a missing star because I don't know why it tasted so funny in the beginning.

I seen that there was many good reviews about this product so I though I'd have nothing to lose. So when it was delivered to me, this was the first of 2 coffees I had opened. Upon opening of the bag, it had the smell I was looking for in a coffee bean. So anyway, I drink my coffee with milk based cream, and organic turbinado sugar, so this review may not be for you. After brewing (French Press) and upon my first sip, there was a peculiar taste and finish to it. So I looked on the label and it had said "50% Honduran Peaberry / 50% Guatemalan San Antonio" but still said "Medium-Dark Roast" and immediately I said to myself "wait a minute, that's not what I ordered". I looked at my order and on the bag it said "Honduran Marcala". But that's not the reason for the 3 stars (for it's possible that they use different beans from different areas to maintain the "Medium-Dark Roast" type coffee).
The coffee after brewing was extremely "earthy", so much it left an odd taste during and after finishing a sip. So maybe it is because of the type of bean, and/or it's something I'm not used to. I just wasn't ready for that kind of change in how I prefer my coffee as far as taste. So I'm not necessarily saying it is a bad coffee, I just wasn't ready, and probably won't be willing to deal with the taste.

title: V14
text:
This is probably the very finest bottled vegetable juice I've ever tried. And although it's available locally, the six-pack sold through Amazon seems to offer about the best available price.

As my review title suggests, you get not eight, not ten, not twelve, but _fourteen_ kinds of veggie juice in this mix. And you can taste pretty much all of them. Just chill a bottle of it in your fridge, pour a glass, toss it at your tonsils, and wait; aha, there's the tomato, and there's the carrot, and there's the broccoli . . .

What I usually do with bottled/canned vegetable juice is to modify it myself with a dash (or six) of hot pepper sauce, some lemon juice, a bit of salt, and a healthy dollop of Worcestershire sauce. Well, I tried that with this juice and found that I liked it _better_ without my own modifications. This is a nice, flavorful, carefully balanced mix, and my tinkering didn't improve it.[*]

Which is good for another reason: this stuff is pretty low in salt, and it relies on pepper and garlic to give it a little bite. So if you're watching your sodium, you'll be glad to know that one 8-oz. glass includes just 4% of your RDA and doesn't require supplementation in order to taste good.

Good juice.

(The product image shown on this page at the time I'm writing is a little weird-looking; it makes the juice look orange, which it isn't. The predominant ingredient is tomato juice, and that's what this stuff looks like.)

----

[*] However, I've discovered since writing this review that I do like to add a splash of [[ASIN:B001M1DUDU Lakewood Organic PURE Lemon Juice, 12.5-Ounce Bottles (Pack of 12)]] or [[ASIN:B001M1IQ3Y Lakewood Organic PURE Lime Juice, 12.5-Ounce Bottles (Pack of 12)]]. Also, even though it contains celery juice, it's good with a dash of [[ASIN:B001XWNBWI Simply Organic Celery Salt Certified Organic, 5.54-Ounce Containers (Pack of 3)]] as well.

title: Good Chew.  Great flavor after 3 days in fridge.
text: This is a very good pizza flour.  I mix using 500g flour to 350g of water, 1 tsp salt  1 tsp or less of yeast.  Mix for 6 mins with dough hook.  Cover and put in Fridge for 3 days to set up.  It will slightly ferment this way, it's a cold rise.  On pizza day, I put 2 or more cups of water in  microwave for 6 mins to get water boiling.  Then turn microwave off.  Then put container with dough from fridge into microwave and let it set for an hour or two for final rise and the steam inside will be exactly right proofing temp, and the dough will be perfect.  Dust with flour and make two or three pizza's.  Put into very hot oven (I use gas grill with a pizza oven cover kit and pizza stone for higher 800F temp).  Crust bubbles and chars around outside (where you don't put sauce) and looks and tastes absolutely professional.  Use a 9 inch round pizza peal to turn the pizza inside the oven, peal should have long handle.  Peal is sold on amazon.  The Grill insert for pizza is sold on Amazon.  Good Luck!

title: The leaves are acceptable - the Earl Grey flavor is weak
text:
I bought this tea because I avoid caffeine for health reasons, but really love the flavor of Earl Grey. I'm a big fan of rooibos as a substitute for standard tea, and thought this idea held a lot of promise. Well... I still think the idea holds a lot of promise but I don't think this is a very good realization of that. The leaves themselves are about what you'd expect from a budget rooibos, pretty fine and likely to slip through your steeper at least a little bit. Hard to blame them too much on that account because unfortunately that's just how rooibos is, it has much smaller needly leaves as opposed to big unfurling tea leaves.

The Earl Grey flavor leaves a lot to be desired. I've brewed this a few times with my girlfriend and we've both decided it mostly tastes just like a standard unflavored rooibos. There is a hint of the distinctive bergamot, but barely enough to make a difference in flavor, regardless of the strength you brew it at. Of course part of the distinctive Earl Grey flavor in a traditional Earl Grey comes from the tea itself, and I would never hold that against them. I haven't found any better options on Amazon yet. I'm considering buying some essence of bergamot and trying to make some myself, although the prospect is a little intimidating.

title: Excellent blending coffee for espresso -- a way to get Robusta flavor and crema into your mix.
text:
If you use this straight for espresso, it will produce coffee very similar to what you get at a coffee bar in Italy. Which makes sense since Lavazza is the biggest supplier of coffee in Italy.

It's a robusta-heavy blend (about 70%) so it produces very strong crema but it doesn't have the sweetness of a good arabica.

We mix this coffee about 50-50 with dark roast (usually Starbucks or Costco/Kirkland). It's a crema booster but also gives you a few extra notes of flavor that you don't get from arabica alone.

The price is also a bonus. If you buy these in bulk, the price per pound is much less than what you'd have to pay for a decent robusta (especially since robusta is not very popular or widely distributed in the US).

title: Old Bru
text: I love Irn Bru. From the first time I tried it in Scotland, I loved the drink. But something was off. I just got back from another trip to the UK, and brought a couple Irn Brus back with me, then ordered some off of Amazon. Today, I did a blind taste test. I could easily taste the difference. Then I realized the big problem. The Amazon ordered Irn Bru was almost completely flat. I checked dates on both bottles, seeing Apr2023 for the one I brought back, and nothing on the Amazon ordered bottle. I'm guessing that there's a bunch that has been sitting in a warehouse for way too long. So, if you really must have Irn Bru, and have no other way to get it, this will do. It's mostly there. But if you can hold off until you make a trip, or don't mind paying way more to get it shipped from overseas (or maybe have a friend over there that can get it to you), that's the better option if you want the full taste that you know and love. Note: After writing this review, while the bottles don't have any "best by" date, I saw that they had but a sticker of the plastic that covered the bottles. While this date shows Jan2023, due to how flat they are, I highly doubt this. Anyone can put a sticker on something... just my view on it, based on the taste.

title: Overpriced but decent spice blends
text: This collection of spice blends from online brand "Gustus Vitae" seems pretty crazily overpriced to me, but is pleasant enough if not exactly as special as the price might imply. Packaged in plastic within their magnetized metal tins (several of which arrived dinged) are four spice blends and two seasoned salts. (All the spice blends also include salt, and one has sugar as well.) They're all tasty and decent enough, but not ultra-fresh or as strongly flavored as the ultra-high-quality herbs you might expect at this price point — instead there is a noticeable tinge of the cardboardy spoiled taste of older powdered spices just like the ones you might find for a buck or two at the grocery store. Still, the blends are pleasant — I liked the "Jamaican" blend, a mild jerk-like concoction that it's easy to heat up with additional chile. And the seasoned salts are very nice, both the very mild ancho chile (there's nothing really chile-spicy in this package) and the very smoky smoked salt. There's no reason at all to spend nearly this much on this quality of spice — you can get just as much flavor for less than half this much at any supermarket — but price aside, this assortment is a nice one.

title: Kashi has brought cereal back into my life
text:
When I was a kid I ate cereal all the time for breakfast. As I got older, I started to get away from the cereal in favor of things like whole-grain English muffins. This was because the cereals out there were either chock full of sugar or "healthy" and, therefore, tasteless with a cardboard-like texture. Kashi to the rescue!

I particularly love this cereal because of the honey flavor. It is a nice, light flavor and has what I consider to be the perfect degree of sweetness. Unlike with sugar cereals, I don't have the sensation of instant tooth decay when I eat this one. Better yet, the cereal is a blend of whole grains. I find that eating this cereal and other Kashi products helps me to stay full longer and also makes me less likely to crave sugary goods. I've long been reluctant to let my daughter eat much cereal for breakfast for the abovementioned reasons but she loves this cereal just as much as I do. It's definitely gratifying to be able to serve my daughter something that she not only loves, but that I know is also healthy for her.

title: Flavorful, Good Value, but Too Salty for Some Uses
text:
These olives are packed well, flavorful, and a great value for the quantity. Prepare to exert some patience when removing the plastic insert you'll find when you first remove the lid.
It's difficult to eat many of these olive slices on their own because as others have mentioned, they're far too salty. Some olive producers recommend rinsing their olives before use, but IMO rinsing less-than-whole olives is just gross, and good olive brine adds a lot of extra flavor. I use these almost exclusively as an ingredient in various recipes, so they do work for me; I simply reduce the added salt content of the dish to compensate accordingly.
Another reviewer wrote that the slices are "canoe shaped" - They're actually perpendicularly (to the stone) sliced rings. -I've attached a pic for size and shape reference.
Like many Roland products, this item came with no obvious production date, best-by date, or expiration date. There is an obscure, coded stick-on label on the side of the container which requires you to do some online sleuthing if you want to figure out what the codes mean. After a few minutes of searching online (the link offered in the product description doesn't work), I found no specific chart online for this exact product; I did find another Roland chart which seemed to properly decipher the production date (6-ish months before purchase) , but I gave up trying to decode two other sets of numbers on the tag. I find this practice by food suppliers annoying at best, shady at worst.
I removed one star for the excessive saltiness of the olives which limits their use, and for the iffy shelf-life info of the labeling.

title: Awesome for thickening liquids
text: I love this for making my apple pie filling, which I gave away to the neighbors this year for Christmas.  Since then I have used it to thicken other items.  I used it in my salsa, and it thickened it like it was supposed to, however it was a little weird eating "jelly salsa"  since it thickened all the liquid and took on a "jelly" type texture.  However, the other day I put some in my spaghetti sauce and it helped the sauce stay on the noodles.  It made good gravy.  I definitely like the cook type over the instant.  It thickens as it cools, but I don't get any lumps like I did with the instant.  I made eggnog this week with skim milk and put some of this in it while heating the milk/egg mixture, and it made the eggnog nice and thick and creamy, without all the calories by using whole milk and cream.

title: It was supposed to be a gift…
text:
Pro: Irresistable. I was going to give these to a client as a gift, but I decided to eat them and find another gift. The non-standard flavors were interesting.

One slight con:
Call me ignorant, but I didn’t think not being able to tell the difference between the wrapper and the coconut coating (if eating it right out of the wrapper because of the coconut crumbliness) was a qualification for being “fine”, “deluxe”, or anything else this brand wanted as a part of their image. The packaging budget must have ran out by the time they got to the part that touched the coconutty treats. It may have been unwise to choose uniformity over quality in wrapping the most unique product in the set.

I thought of two possible solutions: Have the wrapper come open still in one piece by thickening/toughening the wrapper material, or change the color of the wrapper enough that customers don’t think of the possibility of eating a torn-off wrapper piece.

The customer shouldn’t be left wondering whether they just bit a piece of wrapper off to pair with their coconut coating. One time my great aunt ate a rock, thinking I had just handed her a piece of candy. Some people might bite bits of wrapper if not paying attention.

Nitpicking aside, this product feels perfect for gifting (even to yourself)!

title: Blue Monkey is yummy and a good value
text:
I spent a month trying every coconut water I could get my grubby little hands on. During my trials, I went to Whole Foods (booooo!) and took home at least six different brands. I got another five from Sprouts (yay Sprouts!), and found at least another seven varieties at Central Market (yeehaw Central Market!!). Of all the ones I tried, the one I liked the most that I could order in bulk was Blue Monkey. I would definitely rank it among my top 3. However, the other factor that made it a top pick for me was the 12 oz serving size and the attractive price point. My orders were always fulfilled on time, and I had a consistent flow of good tasting coconut water. I was actually planning on increasing my order to two cases per month.

Today however, I'm sad because my automatic monthly order for a case of Blue Monkey through Amazon has been cancelled with no explanation. My only recourse seems to be to let them notify me when it becomes available. I don't know what happened, but I'm very disappointed. I hope something changes soon. Until then, I guess I'll buy O.N.E. or Amy and Brian's at Sprouts or Central Market. If it becomes available again I'll switch my four stars to five.

title: Be very careful - might not be safe for espresso machines
text:
I really wanted to love this product. But as it stands now, there are way too many issues and unknowns related to product instructions and contents to remain a customer. After a few gallons of use, a lot of *not great* things happened to my machine:

1) My water tank didn't feed water into the boilers correctly
2) My grouphead started spitting out steam instead of a steady stream of water
3) My steam wand lost pressure
4) The hot water tap dispensed cloudy water with flecks of "something" inside (looked silverish)

I spent over two hours with my retailer to resolve the problem. Here's where I think things went wrong:

1) The TWW packet needs time to dissolve (e.g. don't just put the packet into the gallon, swish around, and expect that the minerals are completely dissolved and ready to be put into the water tank)
2) The dissolving process needs to be refined (putting a packet of minerals into a full gallon of distilled water does not create a great environment to create a completely mixed, consistent, dissolved solution)
3) I spoke to someone from the company who told me that the TDS target was 150mg/L (this isn't on the packaging anywhere) and I still don't know how much Calcium they're adding to my boilers (too much? too little?)

It's a great product in concept, but needs a lot of work for the end customer. AND it's pricey. 15 gallons of water for $15 PLUS the cost of distilled water for minerals that you can buy from a natural food store for pennies.

title: Rich and creamy but gentle enough for your face
text:
Organic Doctor's BioActive Skincare Organic Olive Oil day lotion (wow is that a mouthful!) is a nice, gentle, creamy lotion with a light and pleasant smell.

I had read other reviewers comments about how amazingly hydrating this cream was prior to trying it myself as I happen to have exceptionally dry skin so I wa s looking forward to testing this one out myself and I was slightly disappointed as I had high expectations. The cream itself goes on smoothly and doesn't leave a sticky or greasy residue - which is great. It sinks into your skin quickly and leaves it feeling soft afterwards, a bonus but for some reason I didn't have that "ahhhh" sensation I tend to get from truly moisturizing products.

I'll be honest - I tried this cream on my hands, arms and yes even the highly sensitive skin on my face. The cream was gentle enough for me to use it on my face multiple times without any irritation (a huge bonus) and it left my skin soft and supple and was great under makeup. It left my hands feeling the same way but didn't really do much on the thicker skin on my arms.

Would I rush to buy this product again - maybe but probably not as I like to have a body cream that I can feel penetrating my skin or a face cream I feel is gentle but also has what I need to fight aging skin.

Overall, I did like the Organic Skindoctor cream and I liked that it seemed to be made from organic products bit it just didn't have that "it" factor that would make me buy it again and again.

title: Makes great popcorn, but door hardware could be sturdier.
text:
I purchased this item over a year and a half ago, and we have made popcorn in it about 3 times a month.

First, it does make GREAT popcorn. I have no complaints about that.

However, the door hardware is shoddy and has fallen off. We've had to make some repairs to it. There are little plastic piece that hold the screws and hinges together and they have both broken. Likewise, the little magnet piece at the top that holds the door shut has also come off.

Finally, although most of the metal parts of the machine have resisted corrosion. The metal "ceiling" (i.e., the inside of the top of the machine) has a lot of discoloration, no doubt due to the moisture and salt. It doesn't seem like it's made out of the same type of metal as the rest of the parts. I don't think it's a safety hazard or anything, but it's definitely unsightly.

So, sorry, but I only give this one 3 stars.

title: My new gluten free go-to snack - just love these.
text: These are just fabulous.  I did not purchase them from amazon.  I just spotted them at a local store food store and decided to give them a try then I went on amazon to see what others thought of this item and to see what others were spreading on them.  Locally I paid 99 cents for one 3.5 oz. package.  My husband and I were consuming the organic brown rice cakes by Lundberg which cost $3.68 for 8.5 oz. from EarthFare.  Rice cakes are great with peanut butter for a gluten free snack or meal.  I just lovvvvvveeee these thin corn cakes a thousand times better.  They stay in one piece so much better than the regular rice cakes.  So far I have tried them with peanut butter.  Then with manuka honey for a sweet treat.  Then I also combined both peanut butter and honey.  There are so many possibilities - goat cheese, kefir cheese, jams, sardines, bone marrow - anything you would put on toasted bread but without the wheat and gluten. I think that there aren't many reviews because the cost is a bit high on amazon and you have to buy a box of 12.  Its hard to buy a box of 12 if you have never tasted them.  Also when amazon offers free shipping - the shipping fees are hidden in the price.  I am sorry but there is no such thing as free shipping. But if you want the convenience of having these delivered to your door - just go for it.

text:
My husband got me a Mr Coffee Latte Machine and these flavors for Christmas, so we have been trying them out. Overall, the packing is beautiful, but I am not very impressed with the flavors, which surprises me given most of the reviews thought they were great.

I thought the eggnog was gross, ended up tossing that cup and making a new latte with a different flavor.

The peppermint I used in hot chocolate. It was just ok. I could take it or leave it, which is disappointing. It makes me think I will have to use it just because it is there, not because I will ever crave it. The flavor was just "okay".

THe Gingerbread was great! I really liked this one. I used it in a latte and in hot chocolate and it tasted amazing in both.

THe reason for the 2 star rating is this: the packaging was great, shipping was fast, and I liked the Gingerbread. However, the other two syrups which were 2/3 of the cost of the set I thought were not worth the price. THe eggnog is for sure getting taken to work and someone else can have it. I won't ever use it. Overall, disappointed. I really wanted something similar to coffeehouse drinks to start saving money not buying them.

Edit: after continuing use, I downgraded from 2 to 1 star. I have tried the peppermint several more times trying to find a way to make it good, but I really just don't like it. So I am down to one bottle out of 3 that is good.

title: Just Get that Jacked Apple Hitter, Jack
text:
This is my first purchase of this product, and I went with the jacked apple flavor. Off the bat, the jacked apple is delicious. It has a nice tart bite to it without any sort or medicine-y after taste. For strength comparison, I would say 1 oz of Xmode is equal to a single serving of the standard strength 5 hr energy.

I've been taking Xmode daily for about a week now. Normally my caffeine intake is 2 cups of coffee early in the morning, another after lunch, and some preworkout around 6 pm on gym days (plus lots of water). So far with Xmode, I've completely cut out the coffee, and I have less jitters throughout the day. title: A step in the right perfection
text:
5:45 a.m. The alarm just went off. You want to be on the road before 7. You find the kitchen, get out the kettle and start the water boiling. Get out the Boodum, fill it up. Wait. Water boils. Pour it in the press. Wait. Wait more. Can't wait any longer. Push plunger, drink, coffee is weak, pillow starts calling your name, you lose the will to shower, next thing you know, it's 8:15 and you're praying for the grid to melt down.

OR, you get up at 5:45 a.m., drop a K-Cup in your Keurig, push a button and your cup runneth over (especially if you accidentally pushed the button with the picture of the mug on it). And if it's San Francisco Bay Fog Cutter, you also get a deliciously rich, full-bodied, fragrant brew that is acid free and gentle on an early morning tummy. Best of all, you can drink your Fog Cutter while waiting for the stuff in the Boodum Coffee Press to be ready. Now you can face the shower, the hair dryer, the curling iron and the eyelash curler without fear.

I prefer the Boodum to the Keurig, but when you need coffee now, this blend can't be beat. It's the best of all the K-Cup offerings that I've tried, and I've tried everything from Donut Shop to Newman's Own and most points in between. It is my early morning wake up favorite.

I was very amused, not to say impressed, by one reviewers comments about the packaging He notes that there is a drawing of a K-Cup type machine on the front of the box and a list of various K-Cup brewers that will accommodate this version of the K-Cup. He points out that the San Francisco Bay Coffee supports many environmental projects, as noted on the top of the box, which also shows photos of these worthy projects. The Rodgers Family, who own the company, are shown in a family photo on one side flap, along with an essay on the company's values. The other flap has a description of the actual coffee. This guy is a whiz in the a.m. I'm happy if I find the sink on the first try.

Anyway, this is the best pre-coffee coffee I've ever had. And it's an excellent main course coffee too.

Enjoy.

They are huge when cooked. I drained out the water by pouring them into a colander and rinsing off. then, sliced the large sheets of rubbery 'shrooms into long, thin strips for stir frying, adding to pasta when cooked again, or made into a healing yummy, and spicy, soup. They almost reminded me of large bat-wings. It was crazy. Next time I will remember to not add so much to the pot. These can be reconstituted, cooked, and frozen for added cooking later too. She and I have VERY different scent preferences, so if she ALSO smelled diarrhea without any prompting, it REALLY must smell bad.

The coffee isn’t out of date or anything. It’s packed nicely. The issue is purely the coffee itself. So, I guess it’s worth trying if you want something different from the usual coffee flavors (like I did), but…just be aware that there’s a possibility you’re one of us lucky folks who will smell something VERRRRRRY gross (maybe it’s like the gene that makes some people taste soap when they eat cilantro???)

title: Tastes like Fruity Pebbles only better and holds crunch!
text:
I love this! I read all the reviews saying it tastes chemically and too “fake” sugary, but I have to be honest... if you could or wanted to eat the cereals loaded with sugar with tons of carbs that contribute to weight gain... you would! You have to realize this is an attempt on a company to make something that is low carb and sugar free, so you cannot expect it to taste just like or better than regular fruity pebbles or the like. To me it tastes better! And it holds its crunch, while FB gets soggy fast. It is very sugary, but so is the real stuff and I think it really taste great. The portion size is small, but it does fill you up as there is not as much air around it as most cereals. I eat it for breakfast and sometimes when I want a sweet snack. I do agree with the other comments that it is a bit high priced and the box is small. I would like to see the company make the box bigger and price it more competitively, but in the end ALL keto and low carb food is higher priced so It doesn’t make me feel the company isn’t working within the industry standard.

I have bought the other flavors but have not tried them yet, as I keep going to this one because it’s so good.

I do not taste any chemical taste at all. Not sure what that’s about. That isn’t my experience, but it is sweet, so if you don’t like sweet maybe get another brand or a different flavor from Highkey and try it.

All the Highkey products are good. I love the cauliflower mash! I live on that!

title: Love the taste, but bad side effects for me
text:
This DOES have a warning label on it that says, "Not recommended for daily use beyond 4-6 weeks" and that is VERY true.

I was drinking 3-5 cups of this a day during my work shifts. Great taste, one of my favorites really. However, about 1-2 weeks after starting regular consumption, I started to experience strange things. I developed a Globus sensation in my throat, and sometimes had dry mouth while other times I felt as though my mouth was almost sweating. My tongue gained a white coating and lumps, and overall it was just wildly uncomfortable.

Cut to almost two weeks later, still experiencing the same unpleasant things, I noticed that just above my lip there were two spots of skin that were starting to dry out and turn red. And it hit me: that's where my mug hits when I'm drinking tea. And I've been drinking the tea this whole time--hadn't occurred to me at all that it could be causing these things. So, I stop drinking the tea, and two days later, everything in my mouth and throat goes back to normal.

Now, I didn't actually visit a doctor during this so I can't say 100% sure that it was the tea, but when the symptoms started about a week after I began drinking the tea daily and then cleared up two days after I stopped - I truly believe there is something in this tea that can cause rough allergic reactions. I've spoken to people about it and their best guesses are the Licorice or Eucalyptus, but I do not know for sure.

Consume with caution!!

title: Try before you buy- lesson learned.
text:
So, I absolutely LOVE the Kodiak Cakes brownies, muffins, and pancakes in a cup (though the pancake is the weakest imo but that's another subject). Unfortunately, most of those clock in around 300 calories, which is makes them kind of hard to fit into my current diet.

I've seen this brand at the store before but had never tried them. Saw them here on Amazon while having a huge chocolate craving, and ordered a box, thinking that they'd be similar to the Kodiak Cakes. Boy, was I wrong.

Look, flavor is really subjective, so I don't know what to rate these as. I think they are just absolutely AWFUL, but of course a lot of other people like or even love these. So my suggestion is don't buy a whole case of these like I did- find them as singles in the grocery store if you can, and try them first. Because now I am stuck with a bunch of nasty, awful muffins.

I have been counting calories and losing weight for a few years now, and I am no stranger to diet or sugar free food. Artificial sweeteners normally don't bother me and honestly I don't think that's what bothers me about these. It's just that they have almost no flavor, super weird. I will give them this- at 230 calories, 20g of protein, and a decent serving of fiber, the nutritional content is great. I really wish I liked these. But sadly I do not.

Giving them 3 stars- the price for buying them on Amazon is cheaper than what you'd get at the grocery store usually, and I like the macros. But my god the taste is just so incredibly disappointing.

title: Great syrup for pancakes, waffles and baking!
text:
This syrup is amazing. The caramel notes make it stand out from other cane syrups I’ve tried. Uses it in a pecan pie and it really elevated the flavor over using white corn syrup. Several reviewers have indicated that the cans were dented or that syrup had leaked out. Mine was delivered from a local Amazon distribution center and the cans were wrapped in bubble wrap and placed in a padded envelope which was placed at my front door so they had no dents.

The syrup has a similar viscosity to white corn syrup or honey so the golden syrup would be interchangeable with either of those sweeteners in many recipes while adding some complexity to the flavor.

It’s a bit expensive, like a natural maple syrup but well worth the expense.

One reviewer questioned whether this was truly one pound (454g) and I weighed the can before I opened it and the weight was 17.89 Oz, so subtract the weight of the can and the contents are probably right at one pound. Other sellers offer an 11 Oz bottle instead of the 16 Oz can. It’s important to keep in mind that the can is sold by weight and probably contains about 1.5 cups of syrup. The bottle contains 11 fluid Oz of the same syrup. They probably have approximately the same amount of syrup so it’s a matter of preference on whether you want to spoon syrup out of a can or pour it from a bottle.

Well I have to say after looking most of my life for the perfect vanilla bean in the world I believe I finally found it. For over 40 years I have tried many of different brands of vanilla beans from all over the world. I was on the Amazon site about a year ago and came across your product and knew that I have never tried it before. I order 30 vanilla beans in 3 bathes of ten because there was something I used them for. I have been making homemade vanilla extract for over 30 years now. I found the perfect Bourbon Whiskey that is a Ten year old aged Kentucky Bourbon Whiskey that has a price tag of over $800.00 for a liter bottle of it so I guess you would see why I would need top quality vanilla beans to make the vanilla extract. I ran across your product on Amazon and thought I would give it a try in my next batch of vanilla extract. I use 30 vanilla beans for the liter bottle of Bourbon Whiskey and then I place it in a cool dark place and let it age for at least one year. The number one thing you have to remember is to split each vanilla bean from one end to the other for the Bourbon Whiskey to get the full flavor of each vanilla bean as it goes through the ageing process. You should let it age for no less then three months. I prefer to age mine for at least one year. Each one liter bottle will last me for about 2 to 3 years. When I am down to 1/4 of a bottle I would begin to start another liter bottle of it. That is where it comes down to your vanilla beans I bought from you a little over a year ago. That is when I started a new one liter bottle of Bourbon vanilla extract using your vanilla beans. After ageing about a year I gave it a try. I first smelled it and that was perfect. Then I took a teaspoon and took a little taste of it. Behold. It is the best vanilla extract that I have ever had. I know that it cast a lot to make my vanilla extract but you can look at it this way. With just a $870.00 investment after ageing my vanilla extract for one year the value goes up over 5000%. So I really believe it is worth it. Matter of fact I keep my vanilla extract in a locked safe when I am using it. After all it is worth thousands of dollars. So I would like to thank you very much for such a excellent product. Just keep doing what your doing and I will be a repeat customer for many years to come.

title: A nice winter warm-up
text:
I purchased these as a change-up to our inventory of teas, coffees and cocoas my wife and I drink during the cold winter months.

I've read other reviews regarding price. Although I won't include price into my rating, I will say that an item is only worth whatever someone will pay for it. As for these, I waited until Amazon had a sale and pulled the trigger. I got them for around $.75/k-cup.

As for the cider k-cups themselves, I am pleased with them overall. As with some of the cocoa k-cups, the larger setting on the Keurig machine produces a more watery result but this doesn't seem to affect the hot cider flavor as much as it does the hot cocoa.

Flavor-wise, I'd compare the largest setting flavor to a green tea. Light and not overpowering, but the flavor is there.
With the smaller Keurig settings, the cider has a more robust flavor and is perfect for being creative and mixing in other things. My personal favorite is a dash of cinnamon and a dribble of Irish wiskey.

I'm giving this 4 stars because I think that these K-cup makers should be able to produce a K-cup that creates a consistent product at the larger Keurig settings, but I can't knock it too much because the lighter, more diluted tasing cider can be very enjoyable at times too.

title: Fresh everytime.  Great dairy flavor, creamy texture.
text:
I have purchased Land O'Lakes half and half 192# box several times. I also have purchased Carnation and some of the non-dairy flavored varieties. All together I've purchased about a dozen boxes in total. The Land O'Lakes is the only one that has not disappointed me. I always had "bad ones" in the other brands. Many "bad ones". I have never had any in this product. I do not refridgerate. I keep mine in a see through glass storage container on my kitchen counter. It has a lid which is usually off so it's open to the air, the sun hits it sometimes too. I have occassionally forgotten to rotate the product when I've filled my container up so the ones on the bottom have become quite old. Yes, I have used them anyway. I still have yet to find any bad ones. I know I should have thrown those out but I didn't. I got lucky I guess.
"Expiration Issues" seem to be quite large from reading the current reviews, {I can feel people throwing the rocks at me already!), I don't know what my experations dates were. I remove the product from the box and put it into large Ziploc bags as they are easier for me to handle. I also neglected to read the dates! I just don't know if my creamers were expired or not. I thought they were supposed to have a six month shelf life? Regardless, my Land O'Lakes half and half creamers have always been good, even the obviously old ones.
I'd just like to add that I love the creamy, rich dairy flavor of this product. My coffee is like a rich bowl of creamy delight with Land O' Lakes half and half. I do use more than one in my cup! It is my "guily pleasure". I just can't say enough about how much I love my morning "mud pie creamed coffee"!
There is another thing I truly, truly love about this brand. Its the way they are packaged in these little containers. Many brands, such as Carnation, can be impossible to peel back the seal as they are meant to be opened. I have to resort to getting a steak knife and cutting a hole in the top and squeezing the half and half out. It can be quite messy. One box I received had more than half this way. Not Land O' Lakes. I've not had a single container fail me. Every container has opened exactly as it should. I appreciate this so very much. When I am after my morning "mud pie coffee" things can get pretty nasty is your'e forced to deal with steak knives to get to that cream in that iddy biddy cup!
I highly recommend this brand.

title: Not hot enough
text:
Had this machine for ~13 months.

PROS:
- great aroma and taste
- easy to use

CONS:
- doesn’t brew hot enough beverage
- aerocino does not froth non-dairy milk
- wide/bulky compared to other brand’s models

I don’t eat/drink dairy, so I used almond milk in the Aerocino. It frothed well for a few months, then one day it just stopped frothing (would just warm up almond milk and no frothing). I called customer service within the warranty period and they told me the Aerocino is not supposed to froth non-dairy milk. Wish I would’ve known before purchasing, otherwise I wouldn’t have bought the combo.

A month after the one year warranty expired, a power surge in my apartment blew out my Nespresso and it stopped working. Somehow, my $30 microwave survived, so...what’s up with that, Breville?

I ended up replacing my machine with the DeLonghi VertuoPlus model, and my new machine brews at much hotter temps (which I prefer), and is also sleek and more compact. Better all around. Sorry, Breville!

title: I like it!!
text:
Was a little unsure about trying as I only like milk or 1/2 and 1/2 in my coffee. I ordered the unsweetened as I don't like sugar in my coffee and try to minimize sugar intake. I had read about the product and was willing to give it a shot though to see if the health benefits were worth it.
I added a small amount of coffee to my mug and added the creamer let set a few seconds and stirred, it blended much easier than some folks would lead you to believe, no real issues there.
I tried my coffee and was pleasantly surprised, a nice nutty flavor and not too coconutty or sweet, I wouldn't want it any sweeter for sure. I'm not a huge coconut person but it isn't overwhelming.
For people expecting this to be a dairy creamer replacement, it's NOT. Stick with milk if you aren't looking for the heath benefits of this product. I have been able to skip breakfast and just use about about 3-4 tsp of this in my morning coffee and am fine till lunch. And I swear I really do feel better, keep in mind this is just a part of my newly adopted diet but I have lost quite a bit of weight so far and feel more energy

title: Not bad for gluten free
text: It is a truth universally acknowledged that foods for special diets can be absolutely abysmal.  Since going gluten free, I have probably had most of the worst packaged food in existence.  Happily that is not the case with these cookies.  On the plus side, they have a very good taste, and taste very similar to Oreos, which was a real plus as far as I was concerned. The one negative for me was that the package I bought had some very hard cookies. I don't know if that is typical, or if it was just sheer bad luck on my part.  The taste can't be beat, but the texture was not a favorite of mine. I broke the remainder up in a food processor to use as a crust for a cheesecake, and the crust turned out to be almost impossible to chew, so I don't recommend using them for that.  If you want a good tasting cookie that holds up well to dunking in milk or coffee, this may be your lucky day! A pretty tasty all around cookie, but with my sensitive teeth, I won't be buying them again. In general, this is a good product line and I do buy their products all the time.

title: Excellent Flavor and Texture!
text: I looked at several low carb or no carb noodles. I’ve tried the “no calorie no carb noodles” in the past and found them to not have a great texture and also to be lacking flavor. These Carba Nada noodles have about half of the carbs as regular pasta. They have 24 carbs for a 2 ounce serving vs. 42 carbs for regular pasta. You can easily fit this pasta into a Keto or lo carb diet. I found them to be very flavorful and was able to cook them to a perfect al dente. I tossed them with some of Costco’s Kirkland Pesto, which is awesome and inexpensive, for a quick Italian meal that was very satisfying.

VIVA LABS CACAO verse REGULAR COCOA POWDER

1/2 cup water

title: The price appears to be misleading. False advertising?
text:
The bars should be fine, provided they are fresh (not sure, given some other reviews). However, the price per ounce for 60 bars (and for other options as well) appears to be misleading. 60 bars option includes 30 packages, approx. 1.5 oz each. 30 multiplied by 1.5 is 45 ounces total weight, which is confirmed by product description stating that it is 2.78 lbs. Therefore if total price $18.50 is divided by 45 ounces it gives us aprox. $0.41 per ounce not $0.21.
Unless my understanding of the packaging is incorrect, it appears to be a false advertising

title: Great For Baking
text:
Smooth, rich, just sweet enough to balance out the wonderful sharpness of this chocolate--Ghirardelli makes about the best Bittersweet chocolate chips anywhere! I have used these chips for baking many times, in cakes and frostings and other desserts.

Match them with Ghirardelli's Semi-Sweet chips and you can make a delectable and rich chocolate treat. I tend to use the Semi-Sweet chips to make the cake (when not using Dutch processed cocoa powder) and then use the Bittersweet for the frosting, just to dampen down the overall sweetness and bring out the flavor of the chocolate. Next time, I might try it with a dash of sea salt and/or caramel.

Great for making chocolate chips cookies, where you can use a half and half mixture. One half Semi-Sweet and one half Bittersweet. This brand also melts very nicely to make your own truffles.

Recommended for the baker in your family!
